messages.author: 64dd3e60f9213f7d
messages.subject: goodness-of-fit
parts:
Hi all,

Here's a couple of questions on fitting models and goodness-of-fit measures:

1.
Are there any hard and fast rules regarding exclusion or inclusion in the final minimal model of predictors whose p-value is just above the 0.5 threshold?

2.
Is goodness-of-fit *always* better for the maximal model than for the minimal one?

3.
If, according to some goodness-of-fit measure such as Nagelkerke's R2, the fit is poor (e.g., Nagelkerke's is <0.1), is the model worth reporting in a paper at all? Are there reports of poorly fitting models in published papers?

Thanks in advance.

Best
Chris

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] goodness-of-fit
parts: > 1. Are there any hard and fast rules regarding exclusion or inclusion in the final minimal model of predictors whose p-value is just above the 0.5 threshold?

I have seen ppl include predictors with p<0.1 when the purpose of the
regression model was to some degree also exploratory or when they felt
they could justify a one-sided/-tailed test.
> 2. Is goodness-of-fit *always* better for the maximal model than for the minimal one?

> 3. If, according to some goodness-of-fit measure such as Nagelkerke's R2, the fit is poor (e.g., Nagelkerke's is <0.1), is the model worth reporting in a paper at all? Are there reports of poorly fitting models in published papers?

That's a question one could write whole papers about (in terms of the
philosophy of NHST). The reality - whether that's good or not - seems
to be that (i) most studies that get published have (some) significant
results with some at least decent fit and (ii) papers reporting poor
fit either slip through because no one notices or get rejected if the
poor fit gets detected UNLESS demonstrating poor fit was the point of
the paper.
> 4. How can you explain that you may get poor fit although all the predictors in the final model are significant?

paste("large", LETTERS[14]) # run this for the answer

Just my $0.02,
STG

p.s.: here is your updated code:

Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "russian")

# Read file
data <- read.delim( 'http://kjc-fs-cluster.kjc.uni-heidelberg.de/dcs/data/syllables/syllables.dat', sep=";", header=TRUE, comment.char="#", stringsAsFactors=FALSE);
# Groups - ignore the bad data for now
#groups <- data.frame(rbind(
#    c("Gutturals", "k|g|G"),
#    c("Palatals",  "c|j|J"),
#    c("Retroflexes", "T|D|N"),
#    c("Dentals",    "t|d|n"),
#    c("Labials",    "p|b|m")
#), stringsAsFactors=FALSE);

# В правильной последовательности выводятся
groups <- data.frame(rbind(
  c("Лабиальные",    "p|b|m"),
  c("Дентальные",    "t|d|n"),
  c("Церебральные", "T|D|N"),
  c("Палатальные",  "c|j|J"),
  c("Гуттуральные", "k|g|G")
), stringsAsFactors=FALSE);

# Null matrix of pvalues
matpvals <- matrix( numeric(), 0, 5 );
# The total number of syllables for each period
ns <- as.vector( colSums( data[,2:6] ) );
for(i in 1:nrow(groups))
{
    # Filter rows with this group
    g <- grep(groups[i,2], data$Syllable, ignore.case=FALSE);
    sub <- data[g,];
    # The number of syllables containing syllable of this group
    xs <- as.vector( colSums( sub[,2:6] ) );
    # Combined test across all periods
    pval1 <- prop.test( xs, ns )$`p.value`;
    # Test across Early and Epic periods
    pval2 <- prop.test( xs[1:2], ns[1:2] )$`p.value`;
    # Test across Epic and Classical periods
    pval3 <- prop.test( xs[2:3], ns[2:3] )$`p.value`;
    # Test across Classical and Medieval periods
    pval4 <- prop.test( xs[3:4], ns[3:4] )$`p.value`;
    # Test across and Late periods
    pval5 <- prop.test( xs[4:5], ns[4:5] )$`p.value`;
    # Combine test results into one vector
    pvalues <- c( pval1, pval2, pval3, pval4, pval5 );
    # Add row for this group to the matrix
    matpvals <- rbind( matpvals, pvalues );
};
# Matrix to data frame
matpvals <- data.frame( matpvals, row.names=groups$X1 );
# Assign row names
# names( matpvals ) <- c( 'All periods', 'Early & Epic', 'Epic & Classical', 'Classical & Medieval', 'Medieval & Late' );

# Русские названия эпох
names( matpvals ) <- c( 'Все эпохы санскрита', 'Веды и эпический', 'Эпический и классический', 'Классический и средневековий', 'Средневековий и поздний' );
# Display matrix
matpvals

# Gasuns plot
data_matrix <- data.matrix(matpvals)
data_heatmap <- heatmap(data_matrix, Rowv=NA, Colv=NA, col = cm.colors(256), scale="column", margins=c(22,12))
# http://seqanswers.com/forums/showthread.php?t=12022
data_heatmap <- heatmap(data_matrix, Rowv=NA, Colv=NA, col = colorRampPalette(c("white","grey","black"))(256), scale="column", margins=c(22,12))
# Different aprroach
# heatmap.2(as.matrix(data_matrix),col =
#            colorRampPalette(c("white","green","green4","violet","purple"))(100))
